To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dehydrogenative aromatization of N-heterocylics with (iPrPNPNi)Fe(CO)2(H) occurs through polar bond control of the transition state.

bifunctional catalysts can dehydrogenate N-heterocyles to the aromatic products through a polar bond control mechanism, where the dehydrogenative stepwise transition state is preferred for the dehydrogenations of polarized C-N substrates, and the concerted transition state is preferred when the C-N bond is relatively unpolarized.

the mechanism of dehydrogenation depends on the polarity of the C-N bond, with polarized C-X bonds dehydrogenated in a stepwise bifunctional mechanism, and unpolarized C-X bonds in a concerted mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new bifunctional catalyst for the dehydrogenative C-N bond cleavage and C-H activation of N-heterocylic substrates and the investigation of the mechanism of the dehyrogenative cleavage of C-N bonds.
the development of new bifunctional iron catalysts for the dehydrogenative functionalization of saturated N-heteroaromatics and the mechanism of this dehydrogenative reaction.
the control of the transition state by the substrate structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the polarized C-N bond controls the stepwise or concerted mechanism of dehydrogenation.
the dehydrogenative C-N bond cleavage is controlled by the polarity of the bond.
polarized C-N bond substrates are dehydrogenating through stepwise transition state, whereas unpolarized C-C bond substrates are going through concerted transition states.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

polarized C-N bond substrates are dehydrogenation-activated and dehydrogenated by bifunctional catalysts through stepwise dehydrogenation, while non-polarized C-N bond-containing substrates are deprotonation-activated and thus dehydrogated via a concerted dehydrogenation mechanism.
the polarized C-N bond is crucial to the stepwise dehydrogenation mechanism.
the bifunctional transition states are more polarized than the substrates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
polarized C-N bond control over the dehydrogenative stepwise or concerted transition state is a key factor in the mechanism.
polar bond control over stepwise or concerted transition states is a new concept in catalysis that may be useful for the development of new catalytic reactions.

the polar nature of the C-N bond can dictate whether a reaction occurs via a stepwise or concerted mechanism, and that this polar bond control is not limited to just the transition states but also the ground states.
